plan: [ This is a private-value, independent-values second-price auction. With rational opponents, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy: overbidding can yield negative profit if the second-highest bid exceeds your value; underbidding risks losing positive-surplus wins. With value 49 (max of the range), bidding 49 maximizes win chance while ensuring we only pay the second-highest bid if we win. Ties are random; bidding above 49 provides no benefit and can only introduce downside risk. Therefore, bid truthfully at 49.0 in 0.1 increments. ]

[ In a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values and rational opponents, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Underbidding risks losing profitable wins; overbidding risks winning when another’s value exceeds yours and paying above your value. With values redrawn each round and a 0.1 grid, there’s no advantage to shading or tie tactics. To maximize expected profit this round (and long run), bid exactly your valuation of 44. ]

[ Second-price, independent private values, rational opponents → truthful bidding is weakly dominant. Bid my value ($22) to maximize expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. Overbidding risks winning at a price above my value; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. With three bidders, if I win I pay the second-highest bid and earn v − p2. No history to exploit and only one round, so no strategic shading is beneficial. Therefore, bid my value. ]
